name: Fake placeholder avatars
summary: Do not draw circular initials or generated profile pictures when no real avatar exists; plain names and useful metadata are enough.
problem: Coloured initials circles pretend there is identity imagery when there is none. They add colour and width to every row, and make real avatars indistinguishable from fakes.

bad.description: A list of members, each with a randomly coloured initials circle next to a plain name.

good.title: Names and relevant metadata
good.description: The name aligned on the left edge, and the data users compare (rating, role) on the right.

why: Names and metadata are what users scan. Removing the circles aligns the content edge and removes a meaningless colour.
exceptions: Real uploaded photos or logos that users recognise are allowed.
An avatar is allowed when imagery genuinely helps tell many similar entities apart (a social feed, a shared inbox with many senders) and it represents actual available content.
A deliberately chosen avatar (user picked a colour or icon) is user content, not a placeholder.

humanReview: Is there actual image content, or only generated initials?
Does the avatar help users tell entities apart?
